findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_signal.py:350-364 `resolve_signal` loops over every entry in `items` and takes no worktree. The docs say an agent clears its own signal, so the permissive scope may be intentional (the owner or coordinator resolves). The intent is undocumented.
findings.summary: `resolve` can close a signal on any task's board entry. The spec says a signal is accepted only for the caller's own worktree, but it doesn't scope resolution.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_signal.py:346 appends `[*signals, signal]`. Resolution at line 361 only sets `resolved_at`, and nothing prunes resolved items. The design says resolved signals are 'not shown' and doesn't give a retention bound.
findings.summary: Resolved signals stay in the entry's `signals` list for the life of the entry. Every raise and every overview read re-validates and scans them, and the board file keeps growing.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_signal.py:389-392 return `signals: []` with an error on the first malformed item. The failure is explicit rather than silent, which matches the no-fallback constraint, but the blast radius is board-wide.
findings.summary: One malformed signal or entry makes `open_signals` hide every open signal and show only an error. A single bad record can therefore keep the owner from seeing other agents' questions.
